steps.what: Select reliable psychology readings and examples for the lecture learning outcomes
Plan explanations of psychological concepts and the lecture teaching sequence
Prepare lecture slides and worked psychology examples

loop.purpose: Draft explanations and examples from selected sources and a teacher-authored sequence
loop.input: Source extracts with page references, learning outcomes and teaching outline
loop.output: Slide text and worked examples with source links and explicit uncertainty
loop.check: Teacher verifies claims against sources, works each example and checks that the explanation teaches the intended concept without stigma or clinical overstatement
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported explanations are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Native slide templates handle layout but cannot phrase varied conceptual explanations

steps.what: Approve the complete lecture materials and student release scope
Release the approved lecture materials to the enrolled student cohort
Deliver lectures on abnormal psychology, cognitive processes or work motivation

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} slide templates first, then a bounded loop for source-grounded explanations and examples. The teacher checks content and pedagogy before approving the exact {LMS} release; live teaching retains full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: New lecture explanations and examples require repeated drafting from selected sources.
tasks.enabler_now: Constrained drafting can offer wording while the teacher retains conceptual and pedagogical decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Psychological findings may be contested, culturally dependent or easy to overstate.
tasks.human_edge: Teach uncertainty clearly and adapt explanations to students' understanding.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft writing; source choice and teaching responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-constrained language drafting can propose instructional explanations; disciplinary and teaching quality still require teacher review.

assumptions: Boundary includes source selection, material preparation, student release and live lecturing; grading and broader course design are separate. Shares are provisional.

s1 uses the academic-literature catalogue category of {OTHER}, supplies selected extracts and page references, and checks reuse rights. s2 writes learning sequence and desired examples within retained time; no unexplained structured content is assumed.

s3 includes all draft correction and semantic checks; s4 checks the finished release. Existing approved materials and templates are reused before model drafting. Missing sources or unworkable examples revert to manual writing.

No real patient details or student personal data enter drafting. s5 is a student-facing publication and binds the exact materials and cohort. Changes void approval; lecture delivery itself is unchanged.
research_questions: Does reviewing generated psychology examples take less time than drafting accurate ones from scratch?

already_counted.description: Review and correct generated explanations and examples

incremental.description: Maintain source permissions and discipline-specific example checks

approvals.approved_version: Complete lecture-material revision and enrolled cohort approved in s4; changes require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes ten drafting and two release hours less three upkeep. Low assumes conceptual corrections consume all original drafting time, leaving release alone. Source selection, teaching sequence and live delivery receive no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions.

steps.what: Initiate classroom discussions with psychology questions and participation expectations
Facilitate and moderate classroom discussions, challenge misconceptions and balance participation
Synthesize the classroom discussion orally and clarify unresolved psychology concepts

tasks.design: Keep live classroom moderation human. No additional software is proposed because this task contains responsive discussion rather than a recurring lookup, record write or distribution operation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on interpreting contributions and responding in the moment.
tasks.enabler_now: No tested mechanism reduces this teacher's live moderation time while preserving the discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive disclosures, uneven participation and misconceptions require contextual responses.
tasks.human_edge: Notice discomfort and invite disagreement without exposing a student's personal experience.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in time or decision rights for the live discussion.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: responsive classroom discussion involves live facilitation and contextual judgement; no labour reduction is established for this boundary.

assumptions: The boundary is live initiation, moderation and oral synthesis. Separate preparation of teaching materials is in the lecture-preparation task; no preparation saving is duplicated here. Shares are provisional.

Checked for hidden lookup, written synthesis, attendance entry, discussion posting and subsequent sends: none is required by this live-discussion boundary. If the course actually requires a written record, measure and add its distinct draft, approval and publication steps before estimating savings.

Native discussion boards and polling can support participation but do not shorten the teacher's live judgement or moderation. No transcript, inferred engagement score or automatic summary is introduced.
Zero upkeep is justified because no new tool or process is installed. No structured machine input or external action is proposed.
unknowns: Whether this course requires written discussion records
research_questions: Is there a genuine recurring lookup or recording obligation alongside moderation that warrants separate measurement?

incremental.description: No new system or recurring upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All live opening, moderation and oral synthesis remain unchanged. No record or send is hidden inside these steps, and no tool upkeep is introduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate and grade psychology students' work and papers.

steps.what: Retrieve students' assignments, laboratory work and the correct assessment rubric
Evaluate and grade students' class work, laboratory work, assignments and papers
Write individualized feedback from rubric observations and student passages

loop.purpose: Phrase feedback from the examiner's observations without deciding grades
loop.input: Rubric, teacher observations, assigned marks and cited student passages
loop.output: Feedback draft tied to each observation and passage
loop.check: Teacher checks every comment against the student's actual reasoning, verifies the suggested improvement and removes unsupported criticism; assigned grades cannot be changed
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing evidence or changed meaning returns that feedback to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Native comment banks cover repeated comments but not individualized explanation of varied psychology reasoning

steps.what: Approve final student marks, feedback and release identities
Record approved grades in the institutional student results system
Release the approved grades and feedback privately to each student

tasks.design: Configure native {LMS} batch retrieval and rubric comment reuse first. A bounded loop phrases teacher-authored feedback; the examiner approves the finished marks and feedback before separate results-system recording and student-release gates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Individual feedback writing and duplicate results entry follow substantive marking.
tasks.enabler_now: Feedback drafting from instructor notes and approved-grade integration can reduce those mechanics.
tasks.still_hard: Evaluating evidence, methods and psychological reasoning is the examiner's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize a defensible alternative answer and give a fair, actionable assessment.
tasks.altitude: Less feedback phrasing and re-entry; examiner grade decisions retain full effort.

reach.task: Review rubric alignment and useful formative feedback

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts feedback from instructor notes; this supports phrasing assistance, not autonomous grading.

assumptions: Boundary includes retrieval, marking, feedback, official grade recording and private release. Teacher is the authorized examiner. Shares are provisional; institutions without duplicate entry have less saving.

Students produce submissions with institutional identity and assignment ID; course staff supply rubric revision. s1 checks identity and missing work. s2 records scores, observations and supporting passages within unchanged marking time.

The loop never selects grades. s3 includes passage-based meaning checks and feedback corrections. Native comment banks are tried first; unsupported or sensitive content stays manual and approved processing permissions are required.

{OTHER} is the institutional student-results system. Native grade transfer is tested before a connector. Exact student, assessment, attempt, grade and rubric revision come from s2 and are checked in s4; missing mappings block the write. s6 follows successful recording and releases only the separately approved package.
research_questions: Does checked feedback drafting preserve the examiner's judgement and genuinely reduce writing effort?

already_counted.description: Approve final marks, feedback and identities

incremental.description: Maintain transfer mappings and sample feedback for meaning drift

approvals.approved_version: Exact student-assessment-attempt-grade mapping approved in s4; any change voids recording approval
Final marks and feedback per student with private release scope approved in s4; changed content or recipient voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes five retrieval, ten feedback-writing and ten recording/release hours less three upkeep. Low assumes no drafting gain and existing results transfer, leaving five release hours. All substantive marking time is retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep abreast of psychology through literature, colleagues and conferences.

steps.what: Find current psychology literature and relevant professional conference programmes
Read current literature and assess methods and implications for psychology teaching
Discuss developments in psychology with colleagues and test interpretations
Participate in professional conferences and question new psychological findings

tasks.design: Configure saved searches and source filters in the academic-catalogue category of {OTHER}. Reduce repeated discovery while keeping full-paper reading, colleague exchange and conference participation unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated catalogue searches recreate similar discovery filters.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved searches and publisher feeds can reuse topic and date criteria.
tasks.still_hard: New results can be weak, irreproducible or outside the course's scope.
tasks.human_edge: Evaluate research quality and revise a view after discussion.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in repeated discovery; professional learning time remains.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: academic catalogues support saved searches and filters; discovery does not replace critical reading or professional exchange.

assumptions: Boundary is substantive professional development, including discovery, reading, discussion and attendance. Travel, conference booking and expense claims are separate transactions, not hidden inside these steps. No new report or personal learning log is assumed.

Catalogue publishers supply title, authors, date, abstract and stable identifier; organizers publish programmes. s1 chooses topics and filters within retained time and manually searches sources absent from the catalogue.

Test native saved searches first. Savings apply to recurring query and navigation work only; the teacher still selects relevant results and reads original work. No model summaries or fabricated references are used.
Zero separate approval work is justified because this design only reads existing sources and proposes no send or record commitment. Ongoing search maintenance is counted.
research_questions: Do saved queries recover relevant psychology papers without excessive irrelevant alerts?

incremental.description: Refine saved searches as research interests and coverage change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes six repeated-discovery hours less one query-upkeep hour. Low assumes saved searches already exist, so no new discovery saving remains. Reading, colleague discussion and conference participation keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use reviewed drafting and native teaching systems around human teaching and assessment.
role.ambitious_version: Spend less time phrasing and transferring teaching artefacts while preserving disciplinary judgement and student interaction.
